transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net wireless technical support, my name is Toby. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hello Toby, my name is Olivia Bennett. Whenever I connect my Bluetooth headphones to my Dell XPS laptop to listen to music or join video calls, our Wi-Fi broadband speed collapses from three hundred megabits down to under ten megabits and buffers continuously!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Good afternoon Olivia. If I understand correctly, your laptop Wi-Fi throughput drops precipitously whenever you connect your Bluetooth headphones, causing severe buffering during work calls. Before we test your radio spectrum, could you confirm your full postal address and your account security PIN?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, it is 19 Lansdown Crescent, Bath, BA1 5EX, security PIN 7712, router model S-Net Hub 5.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you Olivia, that confirms your account details. What frequency band is your laptop currently connecting to on the S-Net Hub 5?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Both the 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz networks share the same network name, so I am not sure which specific frequency the laptop chooses.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Could I place you on hold for two minutes while I query your router's wireless telemetry and channel utilization tables?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for holding, Olivia. The router telemetry indicates that your laptop is associating with the 2.4 GHz radio band on channel 6.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Why is connecting to 2.4 GHz a problem when my Bluetooth headphones are turned on?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Bluetooth and legacy 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi operate within the exact same industrial scientific and medical 2.4 GHz radio spectrum, causing acute radio frequency desensitization.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So the Bluetooth antenna in the laptop is literally drowning out the Wi-Fi antenna?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: If you had read the basic wireless networking guidelines for Bluetooth peripherals, you would have separated your dual-band Wi-Fi channels months ago.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I am a marketing coordinator, not a wireless radio engineer! How am I supposed to know about radio frequency interference?!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am explaining the fundamental physics of 2.4 GHz electromagnetic wave coexistence.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can you separate the Wi-Fi channels from your end so my laptop stops using 2.4 GHz?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, I can split your S-Net Hub 5 Wi-Fi broadcast into distinct 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz SSIDs.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What names will the two networks display after splitting?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: We can name them 'S-Net-Bennett-2.4G' and 'S-Net-Bennett-5G'.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That makes it completely clear which one is 5 GHz.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Obviously 5 GHz Wi-Fi channels operate between 5180 MHz and 5825 MHz, completely immune to 2.4 GHz Bluetooth interference.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Right, that makes total scientific sense.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Olivia speaking, I am leading a sixty-person virtual product launch presentation for our American enterprise clients in forty-five minutes! If my audio cuts out or my video buffers because of this Wi-Fi issue while wearing my headset, my company will lose a four-hundred-thousand-pound contract and I could be fired! I am shaking with stress and panicking!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I completely understand the intense pressure and high stakes of your product launch presentation today, Olivia. Facing a critical client presentation while terrified of technical dropouts is incredibly stressful, and I will personally ensure your laptop is locked onto clean 5 GHz Wi-Fi right now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Toby, please push that channel split right away.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am transmitting the SSID split command to your Hub 5 cloud profile.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The hub light blinked amber for ten seconds and has returned to solid green.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Please open the Wi-Fi settings on your Dell laptop and view the available network list.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Looking at available networks... Yes! Both 'S-Net-Bennett-2.4G' and 'S-Net-Bennett-5G' appear!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Please select 'S-Net-Bennett-5G' and enter your existing Wi-Fi password.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Entering password... Connected to 'S-Net-Bennett-5G' with full signal!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now turn on your Bluetooth headphones, connect them to your laptop, and start audio playback.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Headphones connected, playing a live podcast in my ears right now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: While the headphones are actively streaming audio, run a speed test on the 5 GHz connection.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Running speed test with headphones active... Toby! It reached 380 Mbps download and 50 Mbps upload with 8 milliseconds ping! Zero buffering!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That confirms full line rate throughput with complete immunity from Bluetooth radio interference.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The music is crystal clear in my ears and the speed test didn't dip by a single megabit!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have set your laptop's MAC address to priority QoS tier on the 5 GHz radio.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That will protect my presentation bandwidth during the launch call.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have also locked the Wi-Fi channel on 5 GHz channel 36 to avoid radar DFS scans.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you, that prevents any unexpected channel hopping.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have documented these wireless optimization settings under technical ticket WIFI-88219-B.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: WIFI-88219-B, recorded on my desktop notes.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Before we conclude, what model laptop did you say was connected to the 5 GHz network again?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Like I said earlier, it is a Dell XPS laptop.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you Olivia, the Dell XPS device profile has been saved to your hub configuration.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I am completely relieved and ready for our US client launch at two o'clock.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Best of luck with your product launch presentation, Olivia. You are in great shape.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Toby, you have saved my working day.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is there any other wireless query I can assist you with today, Olivia?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No Toby, everything is running at top speed.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net wireless technical support, Olivia. Have a successful presentation. Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Goodbye Toby.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net. Goodbye.

transcript.text: Goodbye.

transcript.text: Goodbye.

transcript.text: Goodbye.

transcript.text: Goodbye.

transcript.text: Goodbye.
